_comment: BAND-SPLIT. Band-local trainers for band4_upper_meadows_ironwood. `order` is this entry's index in the merged array and is the ONLY thing that decides merge position -- never file order, never band order. Existing entries keep the index they had before the split because the merged array order is the order trainers are placed. A new entry in this band takes an unused order in this band's reserved range 4000-4999, which no other band can collide with; do not renumber an existing one.

trainers._comment_gatec_curve: GATEC-CURVE raised this team from 11/12/13 to 13/14/15. It was the one DIP in the chapter's opposition curve: the player reaches this captain at z=5590, having already beaten the relay captain (11/11/12, z=3757) and Captain Riverwatch (13/14/16, z=4350), so a level-11 lead creature here was weaker than two fights the player had already won and the region read as a step backwards. Still inside spec section 3's 'roughly 10-16 entering this band' and inside tests/test_trainers_data.gd::test_captain_teams_sit_in_the_bands_own_level_range. The band this must stay inside now lives in data/config/chapter_curve.json.
trainers.name: Captain Halder
trainers._comment: SF34, spec §3 Band 4. The first of the three regional captains: Ground-focused team, rewards the Field Sigil. Team levels are TUNABLE and sit inside §3's own 'roughly 10-16 entering this band' -- NEVER player-scaled (§3 says so outright): a player who over-levels walks through him, and that is the reward for over-levelling.
trainers._comment_palette: A regional accent laid over the CAPTAIN rank -- the golden dry straw of the high pasture, and the warmest of the three. All three sit in the CAPTAIN RANK's own warm oxblood family (npc_ranks.json, `#d4a3a3`) at roughly its luminance, rather than in the olive/tan/slate they used to carry. That is the actual fix VIS-CAST landed here: NP2-grunt-wire moved the captain rank to the reserved faction colour, these three overrode `palette` wholesale, and `trainer_npc.gd::model_config()` REPLACED the whole dictionary instead of merging it -- so the oxblood reached the generic `relay_captain` and reached none of the three captains a player actually fights. `model_config()` now merges `palette` per surface, and these hexes are inside the family the merge is there to preserve. HONEST LIMIT, measured rather than assumed: every human rig carries one fused material addressed by a single `"*"` key, so the body palette is the only dial there is, and it is now spent on faction identity. Three accents held inside one reserved colour at one luminance moved the RENDERED torso by only a few points per channel in the cast capture -- these read as one faction with a nuance, not as three visibly different coats, and no hex inside this family will do better. Real per-site separation needs a dial that is not the faction colour: a second material on the rig, an accessory, or a per-site prop. The site's own character otherwise lives in `_why_here` and the dialogue, which is where it does the real work anyway.
trainers._comment_ow6: OW6 (owner: 'the captain to challenge is way too close to where you start'). THIS is the trainer the complaint describes -- OW5D's own note below records the pre-corridor stand-in position (52,-122), effectively at the village. It already moved before this item ran. Verified with OW5-walk's real spine (11,316.6m walked, 37.7min, walked/config 0.983): current site is 8767m of polyline / 76.1% in, ~28.7 walked minutes -- third of the four field/relay captains and well past the corridor's midpoint. No further move made; a fourth relocation of the same trainer without a fresh measured problem would be exactly the kind of un-asked-for redesign this project's own conventions warn against.
trainers._comment_ow5d: OW5D, docs/specs/MEADOWS_MACRO_LAYOUT.md section 10.2: this captain was 'unplaced/near village' (the (52,-122) below was a Band-4-shaped stand-in on the OLD map, not a real Band 4 site -- the old map had no Band 4). Moved to (170,5590), the position section 3.1's Band 4 waypoint list names explicitly for the Field Captain. `facing_deg` (-20.6) is UNCHANGED and is almost certainly wrong for the new site -- it was derived by atan2 back to the OLD village at roughly the origin, and the new corridor's Band 4 geometry is a different shape entirely. Left as a flag rather than invented: re-deriving a correct facing needs the reviewer to pick which way 'back down the road' points on the new spine, which is authoring judgement past a coordinate relocation.
trainers._why_here: The high pasture west of the Rise, on the trainer road up-country (spec Band 4's 'high pasture' and 'trainer road'). MEASURED, not guessed: `tools/_probe_upper_meadows.gd` reads h=0.59m, 0.64m of height spread and a worst local slope of 6.0 degrees over an 8m pad -- a real arena, on the flattest ground in the upper Meadows. 28.6m clear of the Burrow Warrens' mouth at [70,-140] so the dungeon's own prompt never contests the challenge, 133m from the origin and well inside world_perimeter.gd's 235m ring. `facing_deg` is the yaw that looks back down the road toward the village, the same atan2(dx, dz) convention every other entry in this file uses. STALE after OW5D's move -- see `_comment_ow5d` above; ground here was not re-probed either.
trainers._why_t3_typechart_rebalance: T3-ACTIVITIES, acting on T3-TYPECHART's own finding (handover-T3-TYPECHART-2026-08-30.md sec4.2/8): this trio fielded Ground x3, which under the new type chart hands ANY Water-typed challenger a -35% exchange discount for the whole fight and taxes an Air-typed one +56% -- the '-35% discounts are the real problem' the design note names, worse than the tax because it lets a prepared player trivialise a Sigil fight on type alone. Swapping the WEAKEST original member (burrowback, level 13, the lowest of the three) for a same-level, same-band-resident Air creature (duskhush) breaks the mono-type sweep: a Water challenger now gets the 1.25x advantage against only 2 of 3 members instead of all 3, and an Air challenger is no longer taxed on every exchange either. Not a fourth member and not a level change -- same team size, same level ladder (13/14/15), same reward. Verified with tools/_probe_captain_typechart.gd (non-mirror: three mono-type challengers modelled against the real chart, not the same type on both sides smoke_combat.gd's own director draws).
trainers._why_combat_g3encounters: G3-ENCOUNTERS (Fable design contract, docs/specs/GATE3_ENCOUNTER_CONTRACTS.md sections 1.3 and 4.2). G-2 defines an optional per-team-member `combat` override that `wild_creature.set_engaged()` merges over `combat.json`'s `enemy` block for that body only (implemented by the coordinator directly, ralph/G3-ENCOUNTERS-0903, to avoid a five-lane collision on the shared script); this authors the values the contract assigns THIS captain against G-3's five reusable profiles. C-4 (Halder, the Pasture: power): Tuskroot -- the second Tuskroot in the chapter, three levels over Vance's -- gets CHARGER (preferred_range 4.5, lunge 7.0, telegraph 0.6, recovery 0.9, attack_cooldown 1.6, power 8.0x1.3=10.4), closing from range in one lunge, the tell is distance not time. Meadowhart (the ace) gets CURRENT (attack_cooldown 0.7, recovery 0.55, reposition_time 0.5, reposition_distance 2.0) but at the contract's explicit power 1.0, not CURRENT's own default 0.8x (8.0, not 6.4) -- 'relentless, not thin: the no-trick fight is pressure that never lets up'. Duskhush carries no override, C-4's own 'default' third member. All values computed against combat.json's own `enemy` defaults (power 8.0, telegraph 0.55, recovery 0.75, attack_cooldown 1.1, preferred_range 2.1, reposition_distance 4.0, reposition_time 1.0, lunge 3.4), which is what an absent `combat` block still resolves to for every other creature in the game (G-2's own fails-if).
trainers._why_t3_reward: T3-REWARD, owner-direction §14 ('Captain 1: Sigil + strong TM'). Field is the first of the three regional captains (see this entry's own `_comment`) and had no TM in its payout -- every Ground TM in the game came from a world pickup (tm_stone_rush/tm_burrow_strike, opening field) or Mira's shop (tm_rock_throw/tm_stone_spike/tm_earth_fist), never a fight. tm_earth_fist is the strongest Ground TM Mira sells (230 coins, power 1.4, one rung under the apex tm_earthshatter that is reserved for the off-spine Band 4 detour) -- a captain victory now hands over the same disc a player would otherwise have to save up for, which is what makes beating him feel like it paid for something beyond the Sigil. Still buyable at Mira's afterward for a second copy; nothing about the shop changed.

Rationale in `_comment_palette` above: the faction's reserved oxblood was reaching the generic `relay_captain` and none of the three captains a player actually fights. Old values: captain_field #a89a6b, captain_ridge #a3a79c, captain_riverwatch #8f9a86.

Measured against OW5-walk's real spine: nearest spine point is 10143m of polyline / 88.1% in, ~33.2 walked minutes -- the furthest of the four, and already sited at the last patch of walkable ground on the ridge (see `_why_here` below, which measured 43-76 degrees of rock past it). MEASURED: h=-1.51m, 2.79m spread, worst slope 12.8 degrees over a 9m pad, 168m out. 36m from the Field Captain and 46m from the Riverwatch Captain: three distinct places, none of them in sight-and-prompt range of another. Ridge is the second captain. data/items/items.json's own elixir header says permanent stat boosters 'belong in the world -- a dungeon, a captain, a stronghold' and are deliberately kept out of Mira's stock so they stay rare; none of the three had ever actually been placed anywhere in the game before this. elixir_guard (permanent defence, capped by progression.json's elixirs.cap_per_stat) is the preparation reward: a one-time, non-refundable choice of who on the five gets stronger, which is what 'preparation improvement' means for an item that is not a TM and not consumed in one fight.

trainers.name: Tether Patrol
trainers._comment: GATE-D4/prompt 65's 'at least one meaningful optional trainer... competing for attention with the captain route'. Spec Band 4 names Team Tether patrol camps as part of the region's identity and none existed here -- the only Team Tether personnel in the whole back half of the chapter were the relay's four fighters in Band 3 and the stronghold approach's own patrol in Band 5, so Band 4 read as the one stretch of upper-country road the faction had abandoned. `rank: grunt` matches the relay pickets' own convention (band3_the_river_lock/trainers.json) -- Team Tether ranks reuse the Warden's rig geometry until NP4-rig installs a dedicated grunt body (npc_ranks.json's own header), so this spends no new mesh. Optional and unguarded: no sigil, no flag any other content reads, purely a coins/xp detour off the watchtower spur so a player can walk past it entirely and lose nothing but the fight and the loot.
trainers._why_here: The watchtower spur, 46m from captain_ridge (-280,6460) -- the same separation captain_ridge's own `_why_here` measures to captain_riverwatch and calls a distinct place rather than sight-and-prompt range of another fight. Co-sited with the patrol camp prop dressing (props.json order 4000) and the resident galecrest (spawns.json order 4010): the ruin, its garrison, and what they left lying around, in one place rather than three unrelated additions. MEASURED: h=2.42m, 0.73m spread, worst slope 11.5 degrees over a 5m pad (tools/_probe_band4_sites.gd), flattest of five candidates walked along the spur. `facing_deg` copied from captain_ridge's own approach bearing -- both stand on the same spur road and face the same way down it.

trainers.name: Juno
trainers._comment_body_t1_cast: T1-CAST, 2026-08-30, owner directive: use the bodies that were generated instead of dressing every non-Tether trainer in one of two villager rigs. `rival_trainer` is installed, rigged, animated and wired into art.json (docs/specs/ASSET_LEDGER.md, T1-NPC-CAST) and stood nowhere in the game. The entry's own reasoning below still holds -- it argued for reusing an installed rig rather than spending a mesh, which this does; it just reaches for a rig that was ALREADY PAID FOR and idle rather than the villager rig every wayside trainer was already wearing. Juno is the one non-Tether trainer standing out on the road rather than in the village, the warm-up the player meets walking toward Captain Halder, and a bright, confident, non-village body is what makes that read at distance on the trainer road spec section 3 names as this band's own identity feature.
trainers._comment: T3-BAND4. ralph/reports/finding-post-tournament-cadence-2026-08-29.md named an 818m authored-content gap right before Captain Halder (trainers.json order 11, Ground-focused, high pasture at 170,5590) -- the last stretch before the first of the three captains had nothing to prepare with. docs/owner/TETHERBOUND_MEADOWS_MIDGAME_FUN_REBUILD.md section 9 wants every captain to close a learn-prepare-challenge loop; a wayside trainer whose own team is Halder's own species one level down is a warm-up fight a player can read as practice for the real one. Independent (no `rank`), matching Bryn/Mira/Oskar/Tam's convention rather than another Team Tether grunt -- patrol_ridgeline was this band's one Team Tether beat at the time this entry was written (CI-TRAINER-CENSUS, 2026-08-30 later added a second, `lost_creature_rue`, reusing patrol_ridgeline's own 'Tether Patrol' identity rather than a new one -- see that entry's own comment), and spec section 3 Band 4 names a 'trainer road' as its own separate identity feature, distinct from the patrol-camp one. Spends no new mesh: `config_key: villager_ranger` reuses the same installed rig `data/config/art.json` already gives every wayside villager trainer, matching Oskar/Tam's own `villager_keeper`/`villager_smith` pattern -- an outdoor herder's config for an outdoor herder, not a new character.
trainers._why_here: The high pasture between the ironwood tree line and Captain Halder's own field, on the spine's own approach -- MEASURED, flattest of five candidates (h=-5.50m, 0.77m spread, worst slope 7.5 degrees over a 6m pad, tools/_probe_t3band4_sites.gd). `facing_deg` is the yaw looking back down the road toward the village, atan2(dx,dz) from the spine's own travel direction at this point -- the same convention every other entry in this file uses.
trainers._why_team: Both already resident in this band (spawns.json orders 4002/4003). Originally one level under Halder's own weakest (12, against his burrowback 13) -- WARRENS-LAND-0829A: that undershot chapter_curve.json's own band4_upper_meadows_ironwood floor of 13 (test_chapter_curve.gd::test_every_trainer_fights_at_their_own_regions_strength), which every other trainer in this file (11/13/14/15, 14/15/16, 13/14) already respects. 13 is the lowest level inside the band, so it is still a step below Halder's own 14/15 members without being a duplicate of his weakest -- the intended 'warm-up, not a formality' reading survives at the floor.

trainers._comment: T3-ACTIVITIES, spec sec6's 'Lost Creature: track and recover a villager's missing bonded Creature'.
trainers._comment_ci_trainer_census: CI-TRAINER-CENSUS, 2026-08-30. Originally authored as 'Rue', a poacher with no `rank`, wearing the villager_keeper rig (config_key/hair, since removed). `tests/test_chapter_content_map.gd::test_the_chapter_fields_the_number_of_trainers_it_is_aiming_for` caps the chapter at 24 distinct trainer opponents, on purpose, and the chapter was already at that ceiling with no headroom before this lane's three new Local Request fights. Reframed as Team Tether instead -- they requisition the stolen Meadowhart for instrumentation, which fits the faction's established pattern (Farro's own 'Company equipment, Company business' in Band 2, the relay captive, the machine under the Hall) at least as well as an unrelated poacher did -- and given `rank: grunt` and `name: 'Tether Patrol'`, reusing the exact identity `patrol_ridgeline` (order 4000, this same file) already carries. No new mesh either way: both entries already reused Team Tether's own rank-based rig convention (`patrol_ridgeline`'s own `_comment`: 'Team Tether ranks reuse the Warden's rig geometry until NP4-rig installs a dedicated grunt body'); this only removes the `config_key`/`hair` override that gave Rue her own separate look.
trainers._why_here: Deep in the ironwood stand between Captain Halder (z 5590) and Captain Vess (z 6460) -- off the spine, the kind of ground a stolen creature would actually be kept out of sight on. Ground-checked flat with tools/_probe_activities_sites.gd (worst local slope 12.3 degrees over a 3m pad); no authored content within 20m.
trainers._why_team: The patrol's own creatures, not the stolen Meadowhart -- the player is not asked to fight the animal they are here to recover. Both species are already resident to Band 4 (spawns.json); levels sit mid-band, inside chapter_curve.json's [13,16] floor/ceiling for this region.
